lesson.menu_title: It Was Made by Hand — When the Thing Matters More Than Who Did It
lesson.menu_desc: A ceramics studio, a workshop that sold out and one campaign nobody signed -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- It Was Made by Hand
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ana Luiza Sellmann | Lesson 8 -- It Was Made by Hand

listenings.text: Small disaster, nothing serious. The workshop on Saturday was cancelled this morning. Apparently the kiln was broken during the week and it has not been repaired yet, so nothing can be fired until Tuesday. We will be refunded automatically, which is something. The good news is that we have been offered two places in the June group instead, and that one is usually sold out by March, so honestly we will not lose anything. My bowl is still there, by the way. It was not ruined, it is just not finished. Let me know if June works for you.

Ana, an update on the campaign before the meeting. The concept was approved on Friday, finally. The films are being edited this week and the first cut will be delivered on Thursday. The photography was outsourced, as you know, and the images have already been sent to us, so that part is done. Two things are still open. The final deliverable has not been signed off by the client, and nobody has been told who is presenting on Monday. If it is me, I need to know today. If it is you, you need to know today. Talk later.

extra_audio.text: Oscar explains that every piece in the room was made by hand. Ana asks him whether the clay is brought from somewhere else. Oscar answers that it is dug about two hours from the city. Ana asks if the Saturday workshop is sold out. Oscar says that it is, but that a new group will be opened in June.

paras: Every piece in this room was made by hand, in this building, by four people. Nothing is produced in a factory and nothing is bought and resold here.

The clay is dug about two hours from the city and it is left to rest for three weeks before it is used. Each bowl is shaped on the wheel, dried slowly, and then fired twice. The glaze is mixed in the studio, which is why no two pieces are exactly the same colour.

The workshops are held on Saturday mornings and they are usually sold out two months in advance. A new group is opened in June and in November. If a piece is ruined during the firing, and it happens more often than you would think, it is not thrown away: it is broken and the material is used again.
The work on display in the front room is for sale. The pieces at the back are not: they were made by students and they are kept here until the students come and collect them.
reading.source: Wall text -- Atelier Sete, Sao Paulo

gist.prompt: What is this text mainly about?
choices: How the pieces are made and how the studio works
An invitation to buy the pieces at the back
